article_content: On Wednesday, Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas submitted a formal application to join the International Criminal Court (ICC). This followed the U.N. Security Council's rejection of a resolution proposing Palestinian statehood by 2017 alongside full Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank and East Jerusalem. The ICC bid opens avenues for potential war crimes investigations in the region. Xavier Abu Eid of the Palestine Liberation Organization explained the move allows any party—including individuals, organizations, or faith-based groups—to file claims with the ICC, though the Palestinian government itself may not initiate proceedings. He stressed that Israeli settlements in these areas violate international law. The U.S. State Department condemned the action as counterproductive, arguing it harms prospects for peace negotiations which remain the only viable solution to the conflict.

article_content: Mae rheithgor yn Llys y Goron Abertawe wedi clywed bod dŵr wastad yn bresennol yng nglofa'r Gleision lle bu farw pedwar dyn yn 2011. Mae rheolwr y pwll, Malcolm Fyfield, a'r perchnogion, MNS Mining, yn gwadu cyhuddiadau o dynladdiad. Ddydd Mawrth, clywodd y llys gan Raymond Thomas, oedd yn rhan o grŵp a brynodd y lofa yn 1998. Dywedodd Mr Thomas bod dŵr wastad yn 'dod i mewn drwy'r llawr a'r tô', ond ei bod yn credu bod amodau o fewn y lofa yn dda o'i gymharu â glofeydd bychain eraill. translated_content: A jury at Swansea Crown Court has heard that water was consistently present in the Gleision quarry where four men died in 2011. David Powell, 50, Charles Breslin, 62, Philip Hill, 44, and Garry Jenkins, 39, were killed following a 650,000-tonne water influx into the quarry. Quarry manager Malcolm Fyfield and operators MNS Mining deny manslaughter charges. On Tuesday, the court heard testimony from Raymond Thomas, part of the group that purchased the quarry in 1998. Thomas stated water had been 'seeping through the ground and walls', but believed the quarry’s internal barriers were superior to smaller quarries. In 2005, operations halted due to a coal seam collapse. The court learned the Ward brothers assumed control of the quarry in 2008, but Thomas was approached to resume as manager in 2011 after the previous manager resigned over health concerns. Thomas managed the site until Malcolm Fyfield took over in September 2011. The court also heard of an incident during Thomas’ tenure where trucks couldn’t access the quarry due to collapsed walls. The interior was described as a 'total shambles'. Despite this, Thomas maintained the barriers were better than other smaller quarries. The trial has already heard evidence from 2009 and 2011 incidents where safety concerns were raised about the quarry. Fyfield denies manslaughter through negligence, while MNS Mining denies corporate manslaughter liability.

Mae Ombwdsmon Gwasanaethau Cyhoeddus Cymru hefyd wedi beirniadu'r modd y gwnaeth Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Betsi Cadwaladr ymdrin â chwyn gan y claf, sy'n cael ei adnabod fel Mr D mewn adroddiad i'r mater. Hwn yw'r trydydd adroddiad o'i fath gan yr Ombwdsmon yn ymwneud â'r ysbyty yn y ddau fis diwethaf. Dywedodd yr Ombwdsmon Nick Bennett: 'Yn yr achos arbennig yma, roedd yna diffyg brys ofnadwy yn y modd yr atgyfeiriwyd rhwng meddygon ymgynghorol ar wahanol safleoedd ysbyty'r Bwrdd Iechyd. Ymddengys y bu methiant systematig i gydnabod ac ymateb i'r ffaith fod Mr D yn dioddef o ffurf ymosodol o ganser y prostad a allai fygwth ei fywyd ac a oedd angen triniaeth radical ar frys. Ni welais i unrhyw beth yn ymateb y Bwrdd Iechyd i fy ymchwiliad a allai gyfiawnhau methiant sydd wedi peri cymaint o bryder.' Cafodd Mr D ddiagnosis o ganser yng Ngorffennaf 2014. Er bod canllawiau Llywodraeth Cymru yn dweud y dylai cleifion sydd newydd gael diagnosis o ganser ddechrau ar eu triniaeth cyn pen 31 diwrnod, bu'n rhaid i Mr D aros mwy na phedair gwaith yr amser sydd yn y canllawiau. Bu oedi wrth gynnal ymchwiliadau diagnostig, ac wrth drefnu llawdriniaeth. Mae'r Ombwdsmon hefyd wedi beirniadu'r modd y gwnaeth y bwrdd iechyd ymdrin â'r gŵyn am eu gofal gan ddweud fod hyn 'wedi dwysau llawer ar lefel y gofid a'r pryder y byddai Mr D wedi'i brofi'. 'Tra bod ein gwasanaethau wroleg o dan bwysau mawr, mae'r modd y gwnaethom ddelio gyda gofal y claf yn annerbyniol,' meddai. 'Doedd hi chwaith ddim yn dderbyniol fod penderfyniad wedi ei wneud i oedi cyn ymateb i gwynion ffurfiol y claf tan ar ôl cwblhau ei driniaeth.'

Sut mae'r cwis yn gweithio?

Mae'r cwis wedi ei selio ar fodel a luniwyd gan wyddonwyr chwaraeon o Brifysgol Loughborough. Yn gyntaf, lluniwyd rhestr o'r rhinweddau corfforol a meddyliol sy'n allweddol i lwyddiant ym myd y campau. Wedyn fe raddiwyd pob un o gampau Gemau'r Gymanwlad yn unol â'r rhinweddau yma. Er enghraifft, ystyriwyd fod angen lefelau uchel o ystwythder a phŵer ar gyfer gymnasteg, tra graddiwyd codi pwysau'n uchel ar gyfer pŵer ond yn isel ar gyfer ystwythder.

Pan mae defnyddiwr yn ateb y cwis, maen nhw'n graddio'i hun yn erbyn yr un rhestr o gategoriau. Mae hyn yn caniatau i'w canlyniadau gael eu cymharu yn erbyn pob camp i gael hyd i'r un sy'n cyfateb agosaf i hunan-asesiad y defnyddiwr.

article_content: Over 300 bridges maintained by Welsh councils are not in sufficient condition to withstand heavy traffic, according to the RAC Foundation. The organization states £100m would be required to bring these structures up to expected standards. This means only 4% of local authority bridges in Wales meet the necessary weight-bearing criteria. Flintshire’s bridge data was excluded from the RAC’s research. A spokesperson for the Welsh Local Government Association confirmed prioritization of road network maintenance. Conwy Council has the highest proportion of substandard bridges (51 out of 234, 22%), requiring £2m repairs. Powys Council has the most failing bridges (62 out of 1,336, 5%), followed by Carmarthenshire (55 out of 798, 7%). Denbighshire faces the largest repair bill at £14m for 20 bridges (7% of its 280 total). The RAC analyzed 72,000 UK roads, noting some rural bridges deemed ‘below standard’ due to lack of heavy vehicle usage.
